To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed an in vitro assembly reaction for the dsDNA bacteriophage Phi29 which incorporates the connector protein into the capsid and that the incorporation of connector protein promotes capsid assembly.
we developed an in vitro assembly reaction for Phi29 that incorporates the connector complex and that the incorporation of this complex is likely to promote the initiation of assembly.
the connector protein is incorporated into Phi29 procapsids in vitro and this incorporation promotes capsid assembly.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of in vitro systems that allow the biochemical analysis of viral capsid assembly and disassembly.
the molecular mechanisms of virus assembly.
elucidating the mechanism(s) by which the connector protein is incorporated during the assembly of the Phi29 procapsid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Phi29 connector protein promotes the assembly of procapsids by increasing the rate and yield of capsid assembly.
Phi29 connector incorporation is controlled by the rate of assembly.
the Phi29 connector is incorporated during assembly in a controlled manner, and that this is likely to be due to its ability to promote nucleation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the incorporation of connector in Phi29 is a rate-limiting step in the assembly of the capsid and that connector is added to the procapsid after the scaffolding protein is incorporated.
the incorporation of Phi29 connector is not controlled by an obligate nucleation mechanism, but rather by a rate enhancement mechanism.

we have demonstrated that the Phi29 connector can be assembled with the scaffolding and capsid proteins in vitro and that the assembly of this connector complex is required for the efficient assembly of Phi29 capsids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to recapitulate the incorporation of connector in vitro and that the Phi29 system may be a useful model for studying the control of connector incorporation during assembly.

the Phi29 in vitro assembly system can be used to test the role of the connector in assembly, and that the incorporation of a connector vertex in PLP is not an artifact of the in vitro assembly system.
Phi29 is an excellent system to study connector incorporation and the mechanisms that regulate this process in vitro.
